headline: George Washington has moved from 'no restriction found' to restricted: the GW Hatchet reports the international office paused non-required CPT from 2 Sept, citing both broadcast messages, with already-approved CPT continuing under current I-20 terms. Washington University in St. Louis is newly confirmed restricted on its own page (posture on existing approvals not stated). Emory, Smith and Vassar checked clear. Tripwires unchanged: DHS still promising draft guidance with no date, Tufts text unchanged, no new retroactive cancellations, Claremont McKenna still stale.

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Both DHS pages fetched 10 Sept 22:44 HKT: the main SEVIS Help Hub CPT page still 'Last updated: November 28, 2023', old standard; the second page, 'Curricular Practical Training Guidance', still says SEVP plans to release draft guidance clarifying previous CPT documents, no date. That draft appearing is the thing to watch.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Fetched 10 Sept 22:44 HKT: page still modified 8 Sept 2026, restriction text unchanged — 'unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time.' A textual change is what would matter.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: None found 10 Sept. Everything on CPT so far is guidance, not a rule; the only nearby item is the separate duration-of-status rule (effective 15 Sept), out of scope.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still only Davidson (15 Aug) and MIT. No third school has revoked already-approved CPT. If this reaches Tufts, it leads.

context: No CPT-specific litigation. No third broadcast message. DHS's stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the new standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.

runs.summary: Manually fired test run. George Washington moved from 'no restriction found' to 'existing honoured' — the GW Hatchet reports non-required CPT paused from 2 Sept citing both broadcast messages, already-approved CPT continues. Washington University in St. Louis newly found restricted on its own page (existing approvals unstated). Emory, Smith and Vassar cleared from the queue fronts. 1point3acres: nothing newer than the known Berkeley thread. Tripwires unchanged, Claremont McKenna still stale, no new cancellations, no counter-trend, no rulemaking.

Yale searched again across law-firm and press outlets — nothing names Yale; still unresolved. 1point3acres: nothing newer than the known Berkeley thread. Maryland and Oregon newly found and verified restricted (existing-approval treatment unstated). Tripwires unchanged, no new cancellations, Claremont McKenna still stale. Ohio State's CPT page located for next run; Vanderbilt and Yale not retried.

Four passes. No tripwire movement, no new cancellations. U Washington, U Rochester and UIUC confirmed with existing approvals honoured (UIUC verified on its official ISSS announcements page after an aggregator-based placement was corrected). Williams, Amherst, Swarthmore, Wellesley, Georgetown and West Virginia checked, no restriction. Vanderbilt lead still unconfirmed. Yale unresolved. Maryland surfaced as a new school to check.
